- scripts/review_autofix_sweep_reaper.sh:116-166 | severity=low | confidence=3
  flagged_by: [google_gemini-3_1-flash-lite, minimax_minimax-m3, z-ai_glm-5_3-flash]
  PROBLEM: Candidates are picked oldest first (`sort_by([.created, .id])`, line 116) with no memory of earlier failures, and every attempt counts toward the cap (line 143), including runs ending in `reaper_result=failed` (line 166). Runs that cannot be cancelled are therefore retried on every tick.
  WHY: If 10 or more runs persistently refuse both cancel and force-cancel, they take all 10 cap slots (up to 20 POSTs) on every tick and newer zombies stay deferred forever. The trigger needs 10+ such runs and the issue reports 8. Severity disagreement: google_gemini-3_1-flash-lite rated it LOW, minimax_minimax-m3 and z-ai_glm-5_3-flash rated it NIT, and anthropic_claude-sonnet-5_5 listed it only as a hardening suggestion.

=== FINDINGS FROM anthropic_claude-sonnet-5_5 ===
- .github/workflows/review_autofix_sweep.yml:Three earlier `exit 0` paths run before the reaper `case` block at lines 459-474: the provider-outage pause at lines 250-253 (`if [ "${PROVIDER_OUTAGE_PAUSED:-false}" = "true" ]; then ... exit 0`), the zero-candidate exit at lines 280-283 (`if [ "${total}" -eq 0 ]; then ... exit 0`), and the default-branch-unavailable exit at lines 293-297. | severity=NIT | confidence=4
  PROBLEM: The reaper runs only when the tick reaches `snapshot_active_review_runs` (lines 444-446). That needs an open non-draft PR, no outage pause and a readable default branch; on any other tick the reaper is skipped and no `ZOMBIE_RUN_REAPER_END` line is printed.
  WHY: Runs past `ZOMBIE_RUN_MAX_QUEUED_HOURS` stay queued and nothing logs the skip, which contradicts the fragment's observability contract. The impact is limited because the next tick with a candidate reaps them. Suggested fix: echo `ZOMBIE_RUN_REAPER_END outcome=skipped reason=<provider_outage|no_candidates|default_branch_unavailable>` before each early exit.
- scripts/review_autofix_sweep_reaper.sh:Line 135, `echo "ZOMBIE_RUN_REAPER_END outcome=dry_run candidates=${reaper_total} attempted=0 ... deferred=${reaper_total}"`. Lines 130-132 compute `reaper_deferred=$((reaper_total - reaper_limit))`. | severity=NIT | confidence=4
  PROBLEM: The dry_run summary fills `deferred=` with the total candidate count instead of `reaper_deferred`.
  WHY: With 12 candidates it prints `deferred=12`, while the fragment's definition and the line 183 summary give `deferred=2`, so one field has two meanings. Cancellation is not affected.
- HARDENING_SUGGESTIONS (3 related items):
  - scripts/review_autofix_sweep_reaper.sh lines 157-171: on `result=failed` the HTTP status is lost because stderr goes to a deleted temp file. Suggested fix: echo `::warning::ZOMBIE_RUN_REAPER_FAILED run=${reaper_id} status=${reaper_status:-none} rc=${reaper_rc}`.
  - .github/workflows/review_autofix_sweep.yml lines 250-253, 280-283, 293-297: the reaper is skipped silently on these exits. Suggested fix: echo `ZOMBIE_RUN_REAPER_END outcome=skipped reason=<...>` before each `exit 0`.
  - scripts/review_autofix_sweep_reaper.sh line 116 `sort_by([.created, .id])` and line 143 cap check: 10 or more runs that cannot be cancelled can starve newer runs. Suggested fix: rotate the start index by tick.
  - HARDENING_RISK_SCORE: 1
- Pass-1 findings rejected after checking the code (4 related items): tests/test_gh_api_write_guard.py, tests/test_agents_fragment_contract.py::test_instructions_point_at_fragments and tests/test_pr_watch_guard.py are failures unrelated to this diff. Cap starvation was moved to the hardening suggestions.

  WHY: The runs the issue describes (queued since August/September, most likely from PRs that have since closed) trigger the fast exit on every tick, so they stay queued forever and nothing logs the skip. The changelog does not document this gap.
- scripts/review_autofix_sweep_reaper.sh:jq sort `| sort_by([.created, .id])` at line 116, cap check `[ "${reaper_attempted}" -lt "${reaper_limit}" ] || break` at line 143, and `reaper_result=failed` path at line 166. | severity=NIT | confidence=3

  WHY: Today there are 8 wedged runs, so two more zombies that refuse force-cancel would fill the cap, and every tick would then spend up to 20 POSTs retrying them.
